subject: Need some help handling a transformation (inverses?) in a hierarchical bayesian model

messages.author: e1a0962c501fdda1
messages.subject: Need some help handling a transformation (inverses?) in a hierarchical bayesian model
parts:
Hey folks

I'm new to bayesian modeling with Stan, and after reading the forum and relevant parts of the manual (I hope) I'm not totally sure if I'm properly implementing a transformation of a variable.  I've copy-pasted my full code below.

The fundamental issue is that I have a prior on a transformed variable, but the inverse transformation cannot be written down with pen and paper (although it's probably invertible).

To give a simple illustration of the problem, imagine I have something like:

Simple Pseudocode:

data {
    int<lower=0> N;
    int<lower=1> K;
    vector[N] y; 
    matrix[N,K] x;
}
parameters {
    vector[K] beta;
    real a0;
}
model {
    f(a0) ~ uniform(log(1),log(N)); // f is an invertible transform from reals to reals, but it's inverse can't be written down
    target += log(f'(a0)); // The jacobian adjustment
    target += g(a0,betas,x,y);  // g is some complicated expression -- the point is that I need to use a0 here
}


Is it ok to continue to use a0 in the third line of the model, or do I need to write things in terms of the inverse of f?  If it's the latter, then the problem is that it's impossible for me to write down the inverse of f with pen and paper -- is there a workaround?

My code below is a little more complicated than this, but I think this captures the basic idea.  In the above example, "f" would be "log_sum_pis" below.


Thank you for your help!


David






Actual Code:

model_code = """    
data {
    int<lower=0> N;
    int<lower=1> K;
    vector[N] y;
    matrix[N,K] x;
    real<lower=0> lambda;
    vector[K] exp_term;
}
parameters {
    vector[K] beta;
    real a0;
}
transformed parameters {
    real<lower=0> squared_error;
    real<lower=0> lambda_delta;
    vector[K] pis;
    vector[K] pi2exp;
    real log_sum_pis;
    squared_error = dot_self(y - x * beta) / N;
    lambda_delta = lambda * 100;
    for (i in 1:K)
        pis[i] = 1/(1+exp(-a0-exp_term[i]));
    for (i in 1:K)
        pi2exp[i] = exp(-exp_term[i])/(1+exp(-a0-exp_term[i]))/(1+exp(-a0-exp_term[i]));
    log_sum_pis = log(sum(pis));

}
model {
    log_sum_pis ~ uniform(log(1),log(N));
    target += log(sum(pi2exp)/sum(pis)); //The Jacobian adjustment for the above line

    target += -squared_error;
    for (k in 1:K)
        target += log_sum_exp(log(pis[k]*lambda/2) - lambda * fabs(beta[k]),log((1-pis[k])*lambda_delta/2) - lambda_delta * fabs(beta[k])); //Note that this line uses "pis" and not "log_sum_pis".
}
"""

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Need some help handling a transformation (inverses?) in a hierarchical bayesian model
parts:
Yes, that's fine technically.

Just because f(a0) is uniform on some interval, doesn't mean
a0, the parameter of interest is. I'm guessing f() is just
a convenient transform to define the prior density you want.

If a0 winds up being constrained, and the constraint isn't
a hard one such as covariance matrices being positive definite
or probabilities being in [0, 1], then that can lead to computational
and statistical problems at the boundaries.

- Bob
